correctness.rationale: The claim is the exact ordered profile (N2,N4,N6)=(4,13,44) of binary linear reverse-complement-complete words. For even k the required RC orbit numbers at k=2,4,6 are respectively 3,10,36; explicit short witnesses attain the first two trivial lower bounds. At six, five high-potential five-bit states and their distinct RC-low counterparts yield a nonnegative 0..3 local cost, invariant under RC. Exhaustive 64-edge calculation, also proved via balanced indegree/outdegree, has total weight 64. Eight fixed edges have weight sum 18, implying that the 36 orbit representatives have total weight (64+18)/2=41. For any covering string, nonnegativity forces at least 41 accumulated units, while telescoping gives at most its window count plus 2; hence at least 39 windows and 44 bits. The displayed 44-bit witness covers all 36 classes in 39 windows. The standalone standard-library checker replays all finite identities with string and integer class implementations. The proof, rather than finite tests, quantifies over all strings.

originality.rationale: The 2013 archive-era primary paper already defines and solves the general minimization algorithmically, and earlier bidirected postman papers also provide general optimization methods. No novelty is assigned to those general methods. In the inspected accessible 2013 primary full text and retrieved other sources, no binary order-six exact optimum or sparse potential proof or first-even-order nonperfect boundary was found. Repeated targeted searches of published mathematical records, ordinary scientific literature and accessible previous claims found no equivalent statement. A general algorithm might compute the instance, so priority is qualified, not declared settled; possible unindexed specialization and inaccessible historical full text are genuine residual risks.
residual_risks: The general algorithm of Orenstein and Shamir could have been specialized to the binary six-mer instance in unpublished data, code or unindexed tables.

Only abstracts were inspected for the 2007/2009 bidirected general-optimization papers, so full-document explicit special cases remain an unresolved priority risk, not a fabricated noncoverage finding.
A human expert could classify the finite potential proof as an already known dual specialization of a standard postman optimizer; independent priority assessment is not performed.
Public search and semantic indexing coverage is incomplete; a missing hit is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: RC-complete superstrings were introduced as a natural practical compression model for double-stranded probe coverage. The sharp first binary even-order failure of the class-count lower bound is a motivated boundary, and the exact deficiency of three windows is supported by a compact potential obstruction with five exceptional states and an explicit optimal word. The potential certificate supplies a reusable finite lower-bound technique and a nontrivial alphabet-size contrast with DNA order four, where the known 2013 table already has an orbit-count deficit. This is more than an arbitrary new parameter slice or implementation check; no general higher-order claim is made.
